result.title: The Information Limits of Neural Controlled Differential Equations Under Sparse Observations
result.comment: Preliminary version. Further theoretical extensions are under development
result.summary: Neural controlled differential equations (Neural CDEs) evolve hidden states along continuous paths constructed by interpolating discrete observations. Sparse measurements leave the input between observation times undetermined, and admissible continuous paths consistent with the same data can produce different terminal states. We characterize this ambiguity for planar drivers with bounded speed. The set of compatible terminal states admits a leading-order zonotopic approximation determined by feasible signed areas and transported Lie brackets. Its projection onto a scalar prediction yields a computable, target-specific ambiguity certificate. We also study the number of measurements needed to reduce the remaining uncertainty. For nondegenerate planar CDEs, the optimal worst-case radius over deterministic adaptive sampling policies scales as $N^{-1}$ when speed is bounded and $N^{-2}$ when both speed and acceleration are bounded, where $N$ is the number of observation intervals. Synthetic experiments assess the certificate using admissible continuous completions and examine the role of path regularity.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 Neural CDE 在稀疏观测下的信息极限：刻画与同一离散观测相容的连续路径所导致的终态歧义集，用可行有符号面积与传输 Lie 括号给出其主导阶 zonotopic 近似，并将投影为标量预测得到可计算的歧义证书，同时分析确定性与自适应采样下最坏半径随观测间隔数 N 的收敛阶。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「给定稀疏证据时 latent 终态可容许集合」的证书与采样量—不确定性标度，可能为量化 LVR 中 latent 状态对视觉证据的保留程度及 LOOK/STOP 的观测预算提供可核查的借鉴线索，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理。
